chunks: As for what al-Ṣaffār narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Nūḥ ibn Shuʿayb, from one who narrated it, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:
I said to him: Is ghusl obligatory upon a woman due to her janābah if a man has not come to her? He said:

"No. And which of you would be pleased to see, or could bear that: to see his daughter, or his sister, or his mother, or his wife, or any of his female relatives standing to perform ghusl, and then he says: What is the matter with you? And she says: I had a nocturnal emission, while she has no husband?" Then he said: "No, that is not upon them, and Allah has imposed that upon you. He said:"
"And if you are in a state of janābah, then purify yourselves."
And He did not say that to them."

So this is a mursal report, and what we have previously presented of the reports is not opposed by it. It is possible that its intended meaning is what we stated regarding the first report, and it further clarifies what we mentioned.

key_terms.جَنَابَتِهَا: her state of janābah, major ritual impurity
key_terms.خَبَرٌ مُرْسَلٌ: a report with a missing link in the sanad

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl from janābah obligatory upon a woman if no man has had intercourse with her?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling of ghusl from janābah for a woman in the case described, and cites the Quranic command about purification in relation to those addressed as junub. The compiler then notes that the report is mursal and should not be used to oppose the earlier narrations, while suggesting that its meaning may be understood in harmony with them.
